title: Cheapest Crew Paid at One Rate
statement:
There are n workers. Worker i has a skill score quality[i] and will not work for less than minWage[i].

You must hire exactly k workers, under two rules:

  • Everyone in the crew is paid at the same rate per unit of quality. A worker with twice the quality of another gets exactly twice the pay.
  • Every hired worker gets at least their minWage.

Pay need not be a whole number. Return the smallest possible total pay for the crew. Answers within 10⁻⁵ (relative) of the exact value are accepted.

examples.why: Hire workers 0 and 1. Worker 1 needs 7 per unit of quality, so the rate is 7 and the pay is 7 · (4 + 2) = 42. Hiring the two lowest minimum wages (workers 1 and 2) forces rate 7 on quality 7, which is 49. Hiring the two lowest rates (workers 2 and 0) costs 5 · 9 = 45.
Workers 0, 2 and 3 have rates 4/3, 0.2 and 0.2, so the crew is paid 4/3 per unit on quality 23: 92/3. Taking the three smallest qualities (1, 1, 3) needs rate 8 and costs 40.

hints: In a fixed crew, which worker decides the pay rate?
The rate is the largest minWage / quality ratio in the crew; the total is that rate times the crew's total quality. Fix the worker whose ratio sets the rate: who else can join without raising it?
Sort workers by ratio. Walking in that order, everyone seen so far may join at the current rate. Among them keep the k with the smallest quality in a max-heap, and track their quality sum.

explain.intuition:
With one shared rate, each worker demands at least minWage / quality per unit. The crew's rate must satisfy the most demanding member, so it is the largest ratio in the crew, and the bill is rate × total quality. Two forces pull apart: you want a low rate and a low quality sum.

Fix the "captain": the worker whose ratio sets the rate. Anyone with a ratio no higher can join without raising it, and among those you want the k with the smallest quality. Sorting by ratio turns that into a sweep: each new worker is the next captain, and the pool of allowed workers only grows. A max-heap of qualities keeps the k smallest: push the newcomer and pop the biggest when there are too many.
steps: Pair each worker as (minWage / quality, quality) and sort by ratio, ascending.
Walk the sorted list. Push each quality into a max-heap and add it to sum.
If the heap holds more than k, pop the largest quality and subtract it from sum.
When the heap holds exactly k, the current ratio pays everyone enough. Record ratio × sum if it is the best so far.
pitfalls: Picking the k smallest minimum wages, or the k smallest ratios. Both fail on the first example.
Recording a total while the heap holds fewer than k workers.
Keeping the k smallest qualities overall instead of only among workers already passed in ratio order. A low-quality worker with a huge ratio would then sneak in at a rate that does not cover them.

solutions.title: Try every captain, sort the pool
solutions.idea: For each worker as rate-setter, collect everyone with a ratio no higher, sort their qualities and take the k smallest.

solutions.title: Sort by ratio, max-heap of qualities
solutions.idea: Sweep workers by rising ratio and keep the k smallest qualities seen so far in a max-heap.

followups: Return which workers to hire, not just the cost.
Ratios are fractions. How would you avoid floating point entirely when comparing two crews?
